nodes.label: Real ClickFix compromise: the user was lured into pasting a command into Run/ex…

data.statement: Real ClickFix compromise: the user was lured into pasting a command into Run/explorer, which spawned an interpreter (powershell/mshta/cmd) download cradle (storyline 400d4a8d7a2fde07). It fetched a payload that was staged and run from a low-privilege directory. The result was a remote access tool (RAAT) installed for attacker control of lab-robin.

data.statement: Benign user or admin activity matched the rules by mistake. A legitimate script or installer, launched from explorer, fetched software from a known vendor and ran it from a user-writable directory, and a sanctioned remote-support tool was flagged as RAAT. The rules matched generic behaviour, not anything malicious.

data.expectation: explorer.exe -> powershell/mshta with an obfuscated or encoded cradle (iwr/iex, curl|iex) that reaches a newly registered or low-reputation domain or raw IP. A RunMRU entry is written just before it, and a payload is dropped under %AppData%, %Temp% or %Public%.

data.expectation: The URL is an official vendor domain, the payload is validly signed by a known vendor and common in the fleet, the remote tool is sanctioned and widespread at Acme, and nothing is encoded or obfuscated.

data.expectation: S1 AV mitigated the cradle payload successfully, with no execution and no C2 after mitigation. The 19:17 and 19:34 events have separate lineage that is not tied to storyline 400d4a8d7a2fde07.

data.question: Do all four risk events come from lab-robin and the same logged-on user? Does the MAC 02:26:f1:d5:d1:97 resolve only to lab-robin (no DHCP reuse or shared adapter or dock)?
data.answer: Yes. All risk events (the four in the notable plus a fifth RAAT event at 20:34:58Z) are on lab-robin. The S1 asset record ties MAC 02:26:f1:d5:d1:97 only to LAB-ROBIN (192.0.2.10, WORKGROUP). The risk events carry no user field. S1 shows the local user LAB-ROBIN\Robin for the cradle chain.

nodes.label: What lure led the user to run the command (a phishing email in MDO or Scanning …

data.question: What lure led the user to run the command (a phishing email in MDO or Scanning Portal, a compromised website or fake CAPTCHA in proxy logs)? Did other Acme users get the same lure or contact the same domain?
data.answer: During the sandbox session, Chrome visited 203.0.113.19:443 at 19:07:29Z (the page domain is hidden by DNS over HTTPS), and the cradle ran 25 seconds later. No phishing email was found: the only MDO hit is SOAR's own mail. No other Acme endpoint contacted 203.0.113.19 or lurecloud.example between 13 and 21 Nov.

nodes.label: Is there evidence of follow-on activity after 19:35Z: credential access, browse…

data.question: Is there evidence of follow-on activity after 19:35Z: credential access, browser data theft, lateral movement, or new logons that use this user's credentials?
data.answer: No sign of follow-on activity against Acme. There was no corporate or identity contact and no Acme-domain logons. After the lure IP's last contact at 19:26:52Z the only outbound traffic went to Microsoft and Google, and the VM rebooted or reverted at 20:30Z. Any credential theft inside the sandbox could only reach the lab's local data.

nodes.label: Is lab-robin still connected and unmitigated? Is it network-contained by S1?

data.question: Is lab-robin still connected and unmitigated? Is it network-contained by S1?
data.answer: The host is not contained. The S1 agent is active and connected (not network-isolated) in detect mode, group "Acme - Security". The threat was never mitigated and was marked benign/false_positive and resolved at 05:01Z on 21 Nov by an unidentified analyst.

If it is rare, sits in a user-writable path and links back to the storyline, that supports w2. If it is sanctioned and widespread, that supports w4.

It is not a tool installed by the cradle.

nodes.label: Is the sandbox segregated from the corporate network? Is egress IP 198.51.100.1…

data.question: Is the sandbox segregated from the corporate network? Is egress IP 198.51.100.151 a dedicated lab line, and did lab-robin ever reach Acme corporate ranges? INetSim was evidently not in use, because the sample reached 203.0.113.19 live.
data.answer: Largely yes. lab-robin made no outbound connections to private or corporate ranges or AD ports. The only hits were loopback 5985 and inbound traffic to its own IP. It made no DNS lookups for Acme domains, is in a WORKGROUP, and sits behind a VirtualBox gateway. Egress IP 198.51.100.151 appears in S1 only for LAB-ROBIN and is absent from all Acme firewall, proxy and NAT indexes, so it is not Acme corporate egress. Who owns the line has not been confirmed.
